scope: Hidden-state-poisoning defenses, adaptive defense evaluation, false-positive operational cost, and session- or connection-level security-detector evaluation.
queries: hidden state poisoning session level detection availability Mamba defense
LLM defense session survival false positive availability detector
security detector session-level availability false positives

primary_sources.finding: Introduces hidden-state poisoning and RoBench-25; does not report benign session-survival evaluation for a deployed detector.
Reports token- and document-level detection on controlled resume injections; does not report multi-turn benign session survival under a blocking policy.
Establishes the need to evaluate defenses adaptively in their stated threat model.
Shows that false alarms impose operational costs in security practice.
Evaluates a sequential security detector over interactive connections and reports false positives per day, demonstrating that operational or session-like units predate this work.

result: No source identified in the dedicated search jointly evaluates hidden-state-poisoning detection, attacked-task utility, adaptive evasion, and benign multi-turn session survival. Related security work does evaluate false-positive operational cost and connection-level behavior, so the manuscript makes no general first-study claim for session-level evaluation.
allowed_claim: We evaluate benign session survival as one axis of hidden-state-poisoning defense assessment.
prohibited_claim: This is the first session-level security-detector evaluation.
